cards.definition: Having a lot of experience and knowledge of the world, or complex and advanced.

example.text: Firefighting in Australia is becoming increasingly sophisticated.

cards.definition: the full power of a country to govern itself without outside control.

example.text: Algeria has the sovereignty to make its own laws.

cards.definition: To hit someone, especially a child, on the bottom with an open hand.

example.text: The baker gave the dough a quick spank to flatten it.

cards.definition: Unable to speak, especially as a result of surprise or strong emotion.

example.text: Vladimir was speechless with shock.

cards.definition: A small, sharp piece of wood, glass, or other material that has broken off.

example.text: I have a splinter in my finger, and I can't get it out.

cards.definition: Very clear and obvious; severe or bare in appearance.

example.text: Stark inequality is also corrosive to our democratic ideal.

cards.definition: Very serious and strict, showing disapproval or authority.

example.text: He gave me a stern look.

cards.definition: To encourage something to grow, develop, or become more active.

example.text: Praise stimulates students to work hard.

cards.definition: Unwilling to spend money or give things, often more than is necessary.

example.text: Tom is a bit stingy.

cards.definition: Relating to the identification of long-term or overall aims and the means of achieving them.

example.text: Preparing for natural disasters requires strategic planning.

cards.definition: To try very hard to achieve something.

example.text: We all strive for success.

cards.definition: to overcome, quiet, or bring under control.

example.text: Claudio's fear has subdued a little bit.

cards.definition: Lower in rank or position.

example.text: All the other issues are subordinate to this one.

cards.definition: To become less intense, violent, or severe; to calm down.

example.text: After she removed the bandage, the irritation subsided.

cards.definition: Not obvious or easy to notice, often in a clever or delicate way.

example.text: There's a subtle difference in meaning between the two words.

cards.definition: Enough for a particular purpose.

example.text: Everyone has received a sufficient amount of food and clothing.

cards.definition: Not deep or thorough; only concerned with the obvious or surface aspects of something.

example.text: Your knowledge of the subject is superficial, Tom.

cards.definition: To prevent something from developing or being expressed; to stop by force.

example.text: I couldn't suppress a yawn.

cards.definition: To be better or greater than someone or something else.

example.text: Your talents far surpass my own.

cards.definition: Close observation of a person or area, especially by police or military.

example.text: Tom is still under surveillance.

cards.definition: Able to be maintained at a certain rate or level; causing little or no damage to the environment.

example.text: Wood is a sustainable building material.

cards.definition: A quick, large drink of liquid.

example.text: He drank a swig of water.

cards.definition: A group of symptoms that consistently occur together, or a set of characteristics.

example.text: Esther has irritable bowel syndrome.

cards.definition: To end something or to stop it from continuing.

example.text: The contract has been mutually terminated.

cards.definition: To transform a planet or moon so that it can support human life.

example.text: Can we really terraform Mars?

cards.definition: Relating to a specific area of land or water, or showing a strong desire to defend one's own area.

example.text: This is a territorial animal.

cards.definition: To give evidence or make a statement in a court of law.

example.text: I can testify to that.

cards.definition: A formal statement or evidence given by a witness in a court of law.

example.text: The court heard the testimony of Tom Jackson.

cards.definition: A long piece of writing on a particular subject, especially one written for a university degree.

example.text: Have you finished writing your thesis?

cards.definition: A violent person, especially a criminal.

example.text: Edmundo was attacked by a thug.

cards.definition: Severe physical or mental suffering.

example.text: Ziri endured years of torment.

cards.definition: A process or period of changing from one state or condition to another.

example.text: Algeria needs to speed up the transition to renewable energy.

cards.definition: The quality of being open, honest, and clear, without secrets.

example.text: In Algeria, the main cause of corruption is the lack of transparency.

cards.definition: A very upsetting or shocking experience that may cause lasting emotional or mental problems.

example.text: Yanni wants to help Skura confront her childhood trauma.

cards.definition: Causing severe and lasting emotional shock and upset.

example.text: You had a very traumatic experience.

cards.definition: the crime of betraying one's country, especially by trying to overthrow the government.

example.text: This could be construed as an act of treason.

cards.definition: A thing of little value or importance.

example.text: Don't make a fuss about trifles.

cards.definition: A great victory or success.

example.text: The second marriage is the triumph of hope over experience.

cards.definition: A serious infectious disease that affects the lungs and other parts of the body.

example.text: Tuberculosis is a bacterial disease.

cards.definition: A ruler who uses power in a cruel and unfair way.

example.text: The people suffered under the cruel tyrant.

cards.definition: The bag-like part of a female cow, goat, or sheep that hangs down and produces milk.

example.text: Yanni washed his goat's udder with warm water.

cards.definition: A type of light that humans cannot see, which can be harmful.

example.text: The ozone layer helps protect us from ultraviolet radiation from the sun.

cards.definition: Showing no prejudice for or against something; fair and objective.

example.text: Tom told me that he was unbiased.

cards.definition: To remove an obstruction from a pipe or drain, allowing liquid to flow freely.

example.text: Can you unclog the toilet?

cards.definition: In a way that cannot be stopped or managed.

example.text: Tom buried his face in his hands and sobbed uncontrollably.

cards.definition: Not persuaded that something is true or right.

example.text: Tom looked a little unconvinced.

cards.definition: Not reliable or trustworthy; likely to fail or disappoint.

example.text: I know Tom is undependable.

cards.definition: To think that someone or something is less important or capable than they really are.

example.text: Be careful not to underestimate the problem.

cards.definition: To experience or be subjected to something, often a process or change.

example.text: The new engine must undergo all the necessary tests.

cards.definition: To make something weaker or less effective, often in a gradual way.

example.text: Let's not do anything to undermine Tom.

cards.definition: Without question; certainly.

example.text: You're undoubtedly the best swimmer here.

cards.definition: Not showing much interest or excitement.

example.text: Tom said Mary is unenthusiastic about that.

cards.definition: Not morally correct or acceptable.

example.text: It is an unethical industry.

cards.definition: Not surprised, worried, or disturbed by something, even when it is unexpected or difficult.

example.text: Unfazed by criticism, she continued her work.

cards.definition: not based on facts or good reasons.

example.text: However, these fears proved unfounded.

cards.definition: Never having happened or existed before.

example.text: The situation this year is unprecedented.

cards.definition: A state of dissatisfaction, disturbance, and agitation among a group of people.

example.text: The unrest of the crowd came to a boiling point.

cards.definition: The greatest possible amount or degree of something.

example.text: It is of the utmost importance.

cards.definition: To say something or make a sound with your voice.

example.text: I didn't utter a word.

cards.definition: Completely and absolutely.

example.text: Today I am utterly tired.

cards.definition: The act of confirming or proving that something is true, correct, or acceptable.

example.text: Yanni doesn't need validation from other people.

cards.definition: in a strong, passionate, or intense manner.

example.text: Tom vehemently denied he'd done that.

cards.definition: The act of harming someone because they harmed you first.

example.text: Tom doesn't want justice. He wants vengeance.

cards.definition: A decision made by a jury or judge in a court case, or a judgment about something.

example.text: Has the jury reached a verdict?

cards.definition: Able to do many different things well, or having many different uses.

example.text: Chickpeas are a versatile legume.

cards.definition: A bad habit or immoral behavior, or a fault in something.

example.text: Tom says he has no vices.

cards.definition: A good moral quality or habit, or a good feature of something.

example.text: Courage is an excellent virtue.

cards.definition: a completely empty space, or a feeling of emptiness.

example.text: Janos felt a void in his heart.

cards.definition: Lacking sophistication or good taste; rude or offensive.

example.text: I don't like vulgar jokes.

cards.definition: A large bird that eats the flesh of dead animals.

example.text: Where there is carrion, vultures gather.

cards.definition: An official document that gives permission for something, such as an arrest or search.

example.text: We have a warrant for your arrest.

cards.definition: Careful because you think there might be a danger or problem.

example.text: I've always been wary of such people.

cards.definition: To gradually stop a baby or young animal from drinking its mother's milk.

example.text: Ziri wanted to wean the lambs from the ewe.

cards.definition: Used instead of "who" when it is the object of a verb or preposition.

example.text: With whom did you go?

cards.definition: For a plant or flower to become limp and droop, usually from lack of water.

example.text: This weather is making the flowers wilt.

cards.definition: To become dry and shriveled, often due to lack of water or nourishment.

example.text: The flower withered for lack of water.

cards.definition: Using words in a clever and amusing way.

example.text: He's always making such witty remarks!

cards.definition: Feeling dizzy, unsteady, or slightly sick.

example.text: I was a bit woozy.
